statement0:
The word "age" is mentioned two or more times in 25.3% of neuroscience papers' Results sections, as of 2020-2024.

Among 2020-2024 papers containing "age" , 38.2% of reported significant p-values (p < .05) are fragile (.01 ≤ p < .05) - i.e., barely fall under the standard significance threshold. This is a much higher rate than the median Psychology paper (median shown in black); relative to other words, papers with "age" are in the top 91st percentile of fragile p-value percentages (lower = better).
Note, strong/weak p-values highly predict replicability.
statement1: As of 2020-2024, papers containing "age" tend to be published in higher impact factor journals (51st percentile among all words) but tend to be cited less (44th percentile word). In general, this word is positively associated with university ranking, such that higher-ranked institutions are more likely to publish papers containing "age" (53rd percentile).
